claim: S100A8 and S100A9 are among the most abundant proteins in neutrophils and monocytes.
source: The proinflammatory alarmins S100A8 and S100A9 are among the most abundant proteins in neutrophils and monocytes but are completely silenced after differentiation to macrophages.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known fact about S100A8/A9 protein abundance in specific cell types.

claim: S100A8 and S100A9 are completely silenced after differentiation to macrophages.
source: The proinflammatory alarmins S100A8 and S100A9 are among the most abundant proteins in neutrophils and monocytes but are completely silenced after differentiation to macrophages.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data showing downregulation during differentiation.

claim: C/EBPδ was identified as a central regulator of S100a8 and S100a9 expression using an unbiased genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 knockout screening approach.
source: Using an unbiased genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 knockout (KO)-based screening approach in immortalized murine monocytes, we identified the transcription factor C/EBPδ as a central regulator of S100a8 and S100a9 expression.
evidence: The abstract describes the experimental approach (CRISPR/Cas9 screening) used to identify C/EBPδ, and Figure 1 shows the screening results.

claim: S100A8/A9 expression and neutrophil recruitment were decreased in C/EBPδ KO mice in a mouse model of acute lung inflammation.
source: We showed that S100A8/A9 expression and thereby neutrophil recruitment and cytokine release were decreased in C/EBPδ KO mice in a mouse model of acute lung inflammation.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by experimental data in Figure 2E-J showing decreased S100A8/A9, neutrophil recruitment, and cytokines in C/EBPδ KO mice.

claim: Cytokine release was decreased in C/EBPδ KO mice in a mouse model of acute lung inflammation.
source: We showed that S100A8/A9 expression and thereby neutrophil recruitment and cytokine release were decreased in C/EBPδ KO mice in a mouse model of acute lung inflammation.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by Figure 2H-J showing decreased IL-1α and IL-6 in C/EBPδ KO mice.

claim: S100a8 and S100a9 expression is controlled by the C/EBPδ antagonists ATF3 and FBXW7.
source: S100a8 and S100a9 expression was further controlled by the C/EBPδ antagonists ATF3 and FBXW7.
evidence: The abstract states this, and Figure 4E-H shows that knockout of ATF3 and FBXW7 leads to increased S100a8 and S100a9 expression.

claim: The regulatory network involving C/EBPδ, S100A8, and S100A9 is clinically relevant in subpopulations of human monocytes in cardiovascular patients.
source: We confirmed the clinical relevance of this regulatory network in subpopulations of human monocytes in a clinical cohort of cardiovascular patients.
evidence: The abstract states this, and Figure 5 shows RNA-seq data from human PBMCs and monocyte subpopulations demonstrating correlations between CEBPD, S100A8, and S100A9 expression in cardiovascular disease patients.

claim: C/EBPδ binds to specific sites within S100a8 and S100a9 promoter regions.
source: Moreover, we identified specific C/EBPδ-binding sites within S100a8 and S100a9 promoter regions, and demonstrated that C/EBPδ-dependent JMJD3-mediated demethylation of H3K27me3 is indispensable for their expression.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by ChIP data in Figure 6A and reporter assays in Figure 6D-G.

claim: C/EBPδ-dependent JMJD3-mediated demethylation of H3K27me3 is indispensable for S100a8 and S100a9 expression.
source: Moreover, we identified specific C/EBPδ-binding sites within S100a8 and S100a9 promoter regions, and demonstrated that C/EBPδ-dependent JMJD3-mediated demethylation of H3K27me3 is indispensable for their expression.
evidence: The abstract states this, supported by data in Figure 7F-G showing increased H3K27me3 in C/EBPδ KO cells and Figure 8 showing effects of JMJD3 inhibition.

claim: S100A8/A9 complexes represent up to 40% of the soluble protein content in neutrophils.
source: Intracellularly, S100A8/A9 complexes represent up to 40% of the soluble protein content in neutrophils and about 5% in monocytes (Hessian et al., 1993).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hessian et al., 1993.

claim: S100A8/A9 complexes represent about 5% of the soluble protein content in monocytes.
source: Intracellularly, S100A8/A9 complexes represent up to 40% of the soluble protein content in neutrophils and about 5% in monocytes (Hessian et al., 1993).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hessian et al., 1993.

claim: In mature macrophages, protein and mRNA expression of S100A8 and S100A9 is completely downregulated.
source: However, in mature macrophages, protein and mRNA expression of these factors is completely downregulated.
evidence: This is stated as an observation in the introduction, consistent with established knowledge about S100A8/A9 expression patterns.

claim: Expression of S100A8 and S100A9 is controlled by the most dynamic promoters in myeloid cells.
source: This data indicates that expression of S100A8 and S100A9 is controlled by the most dynamic promoters in myeloid cells.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation of dramatic changes in expression levels during differentiation.

claim: Calcium-induced (S100A8/A9)2 tetramer promotes tubulin polymerization and microtubule bundling.
source: Calcium-induced (S100A8/A9)2 tetramer promotes tubulin polymerization and microtubule bundling, thereby affecting transendothelial migration of phagocytes (Leukert et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Leukert et al., 2006.

claim: The S100A8/A9 complex is recognized by Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4).
source: The S100A8/A9 complex is recognized by Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), which leads to the production of proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines (Fassl et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Fassl et al., 2015.

claim: S100A9 knockout mice exhibit decreased pathogenic outcomes in several mouse models of disease including sepsis, autoimmune disease, and arthritis.
source: Accordingly, S100A9 knockout (KO) mice exhibit decreased pathogenic outcomes in several mouse models of disease, such as sepsis (Vogl et al., 2007), autoimmune disease (Loser et al., 2010) or arthritis (van Lent et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to three studies: Vogl et al., 2007; Loser et al., 2010; van Lent et al., 2008.

claim: The S100A8/A9 complex plays a crucial role in host defence against bacterial and fungal pathogens by sequestering manganese and zinc ions.
source: The S100A8/A9 complex plays a crucial role in host defence against bacterial and fungal pathogens by sequestering manganese and zinc ions which compete with high affinity bacterial transporters to import these essential nutrient metals (Kehl-Fie and Skaar, 2010; Kehl-Fie et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kehl-Fie and Skaar, 2010 and Kehl-Fie et al., 2011.

claim: S100A8/A9 is the most abundant alarmin in many clinically relevant diseases in humans.
source: In humans, S100A8/A9 is the most abundant alarmin in many clinically relevant diseases, and is closely associated with disease activity in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), inflammatory bowel disease, sepsis, cardiovascular diseases, multiple sclerosis, acute lung injury (ALI) and psoriasis (Foell et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Foell et al., 2004.

claim: Altered S100A8/A9 expression has been found in different cancer types including gastric, colorectal, breast, lung, prostate and liver cancer.
source: Altered S100A8/A9 expression has also been found in different cancer types, including gastric, colorectal, breast, lung, prostate and liver cancer (Cross et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Cross et al., 2005.

claim: Several potential transcription factors modulating S100a8 and S100a9 expression have been described, but their functional relevance remains unresolved.
source: So far, several potential transcription factors modulating S100a8 and S100a9 expression have been described (Kuruto-Niwa et al., 1998; Fujiu et al., 2011; Lee et al., 2012; Liu et al., 2016; Yang et al., 2017), but their functional relevance remains unresolved.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies and represents a critical assessment of prior literature.

claim: ER-Hoxb8 cells are estrogen dependent transiently immortalized myeloid precursor cells that can be differentiated to primary monocytes and granulocytes upon estrogen-withdrawal.
source: To overcome difficulties of artificial expression and malignant cell lines we used ER (estrogen-regulated) Hoxb8 cells, estrogen dependent transiently immortalized myeloid precursor cells that can be differentiated to primary monocytes and granulocytes upon estrogen-withdrawal (Wang et al., 2006a), and show the physiologically high dynamics of S100A8 and S100A9 mRNA and protein expression during differentiation.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2006a.

claim: ER-Hoxb8 cells show the physiologically high dynamics of S100A8 and S100A9 mRNA and protein expression during differentiation.
source: To overcome difficulties of artificial expression and malignant cell lines we used ER (estrogen-regulated) Hoxb8 cells, estrogen dependent transiently immortalized myeloid precursor cells that can be differentiated to primary monocytes and granulocytes upon estrogen-withdrawal (Wang et al., 2006a), and show the physiologically high dynamics of S100A8 and S100A9 mRNA and protein expression during differentiation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by data in Figure 2A-B showing dramatic changes in expression during differentiation.

claim: The mouse GeCKO library contained six gRNAs per target gene.
source: The used library contained a large mixture of CRISPR sgRNA constructs, where six gRNAs per target gene increase efficiency and enable the analysis of the molecular effects of many thousand genes in one experiment.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental method used in the study.

claim: Cebpd was targeted by the highest number of three gRNAs within the top 20 hits from the CRISPR screen.
source: The highest number of three gRNAs was found within the top 20 hits targeted Cebpd, a gene encoding for a member of the CCAAT/enhancer-binding protein family, C/EBPδ.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: None of the transcription factors previously reported to target S100a8 and S100a9 were found within the hit list of the CRISPR KO library screen.
source: Interestingly, none of the transcription factors previously reported to target S100a8 and S100a9 (Kuruto-Niwa et al., 1998; Fujiu et al., 2011; Lee et al., 2012; Liu et al., 2016; Yang et al., 2017) were found within the hit list of our CRISPR KO library screen (Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and references Figure 1—source data 1.

claim: Deficiency of ATF3, STAT3, KLF5, IRF7, and C/EBPβ does not affect S100a8 and S100a9 expression during monocyte differentiation.
source: Deficiency of none of the stated candidate transcription factors affects S100a8 and S1009 expression during monocyte differentiation, whereas C/EBPδ deficiency had a strong attenuating effect on S100a8 and S100a9 expression, as shown on day 2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: C/EBPδ deficiency had a strong attenuating effect on S100a8 and S100a9 expression on day 2 of differentiation.
source: Deficiency of none of the stated candidate transcription factors affects S100a8 and S1009 expression during monocyte differentiation, whereas C/EBPδ deficiency had a strong attenuating effect on S100a8 and S100a9 expression, as shown on day 2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: ER-Hoxb8-derived monocytes showed about 590-fold increase in S100a8 mRNA expression on day 2 compared to day 0 of differentiation.
source: ER-Hoxb8-derived monocytes showed about 590-fold increase in S100a8 mRNA expression and about 1800-fold increase of S100a9 mRNA expression on day 2 compared to day 0 of differentiation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: ER-Hoxb8-derived monocytes showed about 1800-fold increase of S100a9 mRNA expression on day 2 compared to day 0 of differentiation.
source: ER-Hoxb8-derived monocytes showed about 590-fold increase in S100a8 mRNA expression and about 1800-fold increase of S100a9 mRNA expression on day 2 compared to day 0 of differentiation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: At day 5, S100a8 mRNA expression is about 70-fold downregulated compared to day 2 of differentiation.
source: At day 5 the S100a8 mRNA expression is already about 70-fold and the S100a9 mRNA expression about 110-fold downregulated compared to day 2 of differentiation (Figure 2A, B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: At day 5, S100a9 mRNA expression is about 110-fold downregulated compared to day 2 of differentiation.
source: At day 5 the S100a8 mRNA expression is already about 70-fold and the S100a9 mRNA expression about 110-fold downregulated compared to day 2 of differentiation (Figure 2A, B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: C/EBPδ-deficient ER-Hoxb8 monocytes showed significantly reduced levels of S100a8 mRNA at the beginning of differentiation when S100a8 levels start to rise.
source: Not only on differentiation day 3, but already at the very beginning of differentiation, when S100a8 and S100a9 levels start to rise, C/EBPδ-deficient ER-Hoxb8 monocytes showed significantly reduced levels of both S100a8 (Figure 2A) and S100a9 (Figure 2B) mRNAs compared to wildtype (WT) controls.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: C/EBPδ-deficient ER-Hoxb8 monocytes showed significantly reduced levels of S100a9 mRNA at the beginning of differentiation when S100a9 levels start to rise.
source: Not only on differentiation day 3, but already at the very beginning of differentiation, when S100a8 and S100a9 levels start to rise, C/EBPδ-deficient ER-Hoxb8 monocytes showed significantly reduced levels of both S100a8 (Figure 2A) and S100a9 (Figure 2B) mRNAs compared to wildtype (WT) controls.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The same effect of C/EBPδ deficiency on S100a8 and S100a9 expression was detectable in C/EBPδ-deficient ER-Hoxb8 cells differentiated into the neutrophilic lineage.
source: The same effect was detectable in C/EBPδ-deficient ER-Hoxb8 cells that were differentiated into the neutrophilic lineage (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Cebpd and S100a8 and S100a9 mRNAs were co-expressed in differentiating WT monocytes and neutrophils.
source: Accordingly, Cebpd and S100a8 and S100a9 mRNAs were co-expressed in differentiating WT monocytes and neutrophils, supporting a mechanistic connection (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, C.

claim: WT ER-Hoxb8 monocytes secreted significant S100A8/A9 protein amounts, whereas the supernatant of C/EBPδ KO cells contained up to 80% less S100A8/A9.
source: WT ER-Hoxb8 monocytes secreted significant S100A8/A9 protein amounts, whereas the supernatant of C/EBPδ KO cells contained up to 80% less S100A8/A9 (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: S100a8 and S100a9 expression was decreased upon C/EBPδ deletion in primary bone marrow-derived monocytes.
source: Accordingly, S100a8 and S100a9 expression was decreased upon C/EBPδ deletion in primary bone marrow-derived monocytes (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: S100A8/A9 levels are locally increased in acute respiratory distress syndrome patients.
source: S100A8/A9 levels are locally increased in acute respiratory distress syndrome patients (Lorenz et al., 2008) and have been shown to play a role in neutrophil recruitment during ALI in mice (Chakraborty et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lorenz et al., 2008.

claim: S100A8/A9 plays a role in neutrophil recruitment during acute lung injury in mice.
source: S100A8/A9 levels are locally increased in acute respiratory distress syndrome patients (Lorenz et al., 2008) and have been shown to play a role in neutrophil recruitment during ALI in mice (Chakraborty et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Chakraborty et al., 2017.

claim: Serum and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid from LPS-exposed mice showed highly increased S100A8/A9 levels compared to control mice.
source: Serum and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) from LPS-exposed mice showed highly increased S100A8/A9 levels compared to control mice.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2E, F.

claim: In C/EBPδ KO mice, alarmin levels were systemically and locally decreased compared to WT mice at baseline and after LPS exposure.
source: In C/EBPδ KO mice, alarmin levels were systemically (serum) and locally (BALF) decreased compared to WT mice at baseline (NaCl) and after LPS exposure (Figure 2E, F), confirming our in vitro data.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2E, F.

claim: In BALF, neutrophil recruitment was significantly decreased in LPS-exposed C/EBPδ KO mice in relation to WT littermates.
source: Accordingly, in BALF neutrophil recruitment (Figure 2G), as well as in IL-1α and IL-6, cytokine production was significantly decreased in LPS-exposed C/EBPδ KO mice in relation to WT littermates (TNF-α shows a similar trend, Figure 2H-J), which highlights the impact of S100A8/A9 on the disease outcome.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2G.

claim: IL-1α and IL-6 cytokine production was significantly decreased in LPS-exposed C/EBPδ KO mice in relation to WT littermates.
source: Accordingly, in BALF neutrophil recruitment (Figure 2G), as well as in IL-1α and IL-6, cytokine production was significantly decreased in LPS-exposed C/EBPδ KO mice in relation to WT littermates (TNF-α shows a similar trend, Figure 2H-J), which highlights the impact of S100A8/A9 on the disease outcome.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2H-I.

claim: Phagocytosis capacities were elevated in C/EBPδ KO monocytes when examined using FITC-coupled Latex Beads.
source: Phagocytosis capacities, examined by using FITC-coupled Latex Beads (Figure 3A, B) and by using Staphylococcus aureus (Figure 3C, D), were even elevated in C/EBPδ KO monocytes.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3A, B.

claim: Phagocytosis capacities were elevated in C/EBPδ KO monocytes when examined using Staphylococcus aureus.
source: Phagocytosis capacities, examined by using FITC-coupled Latex Beads (Figure 3A, B) and by using Staphylococcus aureus (Figure 3C, D), were even elevated in C/EBPδ KO monocytes.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3C, D.

claim: Enhanced phagocytosis in C/EBPδ KO monocytes was accompanied by enhanced gene expression of phagocytosis-related PRRs such as Ptx3, CD209a, and Cd14.
source: These observations were accompanied by enhanced gene expression of phagocytosis-related PRRs, such as Ptx3, CD209a, and Cd14, in C/EBPδ KO monocytes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B, D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B, D.

claim: ROS production was not influenced by C/EBPδ deficiency.
source: ROS production was not influenced by C/EBPδ deficiency (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Analysis of differentiation kinetics revealed no exorbitant differences in the quantities of CD11b+Ly-6C+ between WT and C/EBPδ KO cells during differentiation of bone marrow-derived cells or ER-Hoxb8 cells.
source: Moreover, analysis of differentiation kinetics revealed no exorbitant differences in the quantities of CD11b+Ly-6C+ between WT and C/EBPδ KO cells, neither during differentiation of bone marrow-derived cells (BMCs) nor of ER-Hoxb8 cells (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Expression of M1-monocyte associated markers was only slightly decreased in LPS- and IFN-γ-treated C/EBPδ KO monocytes in vitro.
source: Whereas expression of M1-monocyte associated markers, such as Tnfa, Il6, Inos, Cd86, and Il1b, was only slightly decreased in LPS- and IFN-γ-treated C/EBPδ KO monocytes in vitro (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A), M2-associated Il10 expression was significantly decreased upon IL-4-stimulation in C/EBPδ KO cells confirming earlier results (Liu et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: M2-associated Il10 expression was significantly decreased upon IL-4-stimulation in C/EBPδ KO cells.
source: Whereas expression of M1-monocyte associated markers, such as Tnfa, Il6, Inos, Cd86, and Il1b, was only slightly decreased in LPS- and IFN-γ-treated C/EBPδ KO monocytes in vitro (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A), M2-associated Il10 expression was significantly decreased upon IL-4-stimulation in C/EBPδ KO cells confirming earlier results (Liu et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, and supported by citation to Liu et al., 2003.

claim: Decreased IL-10 expression was found in sera from LPS-treated and control C/EBPδ KO mice.
source: Decreased IL-10 expression was also found in sera from LPS-treated and control C/EBPδ KO mice, whereas most other cytokine levels did not differ greatly between WT and C/EBPδ KO mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Doxycycline treatment led to expression of the fusion protein 3xFlag-C/EBPδ in C/EBPδ-deficient ER-Hoxb8 cells infected with lentiviral particles carrying a Tet-On system.
source: Doxycycline treatment led to expression of the fusion protein 3xFlag-C/EBPδ, as revealed by western blot analysis (Figure 4B) and by quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) in comparison to C/EBPδ-deficient cells (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4B, C.

claim: Induction of 3xFlag-C/EBPδ upon doxycycline treatment led to increased S100a8 and S100a9 mRNA levels.
source: Induction of 3xFlag-C/EBPδ upon doxycycline treatment led to increased S100a8 and S100a9 mRNA levels.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Cebpd, S100a8, and S100a9 mRNA levels in doxycycline-treated TRE_3xFlag-C/EBPδ cells were comparable to WT cells at the same differentiation stage.
source: Cebpd, S100a8, and S100a9 mRNA levels in doxycycline-treated TRE_3xFlag-C/EBPδ cells were comparable to WT cells at the same differentiation stage (Figure 4D), demonstrating a positive effect of C/EBPδ expression on S100a8 and S100a9 regulation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4D.

claim: KO of ATF3 in ER-Hoxb8 monocytes led to S100a8 and S100a9 overexpression, especially during early stages of differentiation.
source: KO of ATF3, a known regulatory attenuator of Cebpd expression (Litvak et al., 2009), in ER-Hoxb8 monocytes led to S100a8 and S100a9 overexpression (Figure 4E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), especially during early stages of differentiation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section, shown in Figure 4E, and supported by citation to Litvak et al., 2009.

claim: ATF3 KO cells showed significantly elevated cebpd level.
source: ATF3 KO cells showed significantly elevated cebpd level, indicating a C/EBPδ-mediated effect on the expression of S100a8 and S100a9 (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Lack of FBXW7 resulted in an even higher overexpression of S100a8 and S100a9.
source: Lack of this antagonist resulted in an even higher overexpression of S100a8 and S100a9 (Figure 4G) with huge increases of Cebpd levels (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4G.

claim: FBXW7-deficient monocytes showed huge increases of Cebpd levels.
source: Lack of this antagonist resulted in an even higher overexpression of S100a8 and S100a9 (Figure 4G) with huge increases of Cebpd levels (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4H.

claim: There is upregulation of S100A8, S100A9, and CEBPD in PBMCs of stable coronary artery disease/myocardial infarction cases, compared against controls.
source: Here, we found upregulation of S100A8, S100A9, and CEBPD in PBMCs of stable coronary artery disease/myocardial infarction (sCAD/MI) cases, compared against controls (Figure 5A), together with a positive correlation of S100A8 and S100A9 expression with that of CEBPD in these cells (Figure 5B, C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: There is a positive correlation of S100A8 and S100A9 expression with that of CEBPD in PBMCs of cardiovascular disease patients.
source: Here, we found upregulation of S100A8, S100A9, and CEBPD in PBMCs of stable coronary artery disease/myocardial infarction (sCAD/MI) cases, compared against controls (Figure 5A), together with a positive correlation of S100A8 and S100A9 expression with that of CEBPD in these cells (Figure 5B, C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5B, C.

claim: There is significant upregulation of S100A8, S100A9, and CEBPD specifically in classical monocytes, compared to intermediate and non-classical monocyte subpopulations.
source: Moreover, there was also significant upregulation of these three genes specifically in classical monocytes, compared to intermediate and non-classical monocyte subpopulations (Figure 5D, E, for further comparisons, see Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5D, E.

claim: There is a strong positive correlation between the expression of S100A8 and S100A9 and CEBPD in monocyte subpopulations.
source: A strong positive correlation between the expression of S100A8 and S100A9 and CEBPD in these monocyte subpopulations was found, suggesting that the expression of these genes is mainly associated with the subset of proinflammatory monocytes.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5F, G.

claim: There are significant negative correlations between the expression of CEBPD and its antagonists FBXW7 and ATF3 in monocytes.
source: Interestingly, we also found significant albeit milder, negative correlations between the expression of CEBPD and its antagonists FBXW7 and ATF3 in monocytes (Figure 5F, G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5F, G.

claim: Chromatin immunoprecipitation revealed 3xFlag-C/EBPδ binding on S100a8 and S100a9 promoter regions just before or within the predicted enhancers.
source: Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) revealed 3xFlag-C/EBPδ binding on S100a8 and S100a9 promoter regions just before or within the predicted enhancers (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Transfection of S100a8 reporter construct together with 3xFlag-C/EBPδ vector led to enhanced GFP expression upon doxycycline treatment in comparison to co-transfection with backbone plasmid.
source: Transfection of either S100a8 reporter construct (Figure 6D) or S100a9 reporter construct (Figure 6F) together with 3xFlag-C/EBPδ vector led to enhanced GFP expression upon doxycycline treatment in comparison to co-transfection with backbone plasmid (TRE_ctrl).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Transfection of S100a9 reporter construct together with 3xFlag-C/EBPδ vector led to enhanced GFP expression upon doxycycline treatment in comparison to co-transfection with backbone plasmid.
source: Transfection of either S100a8 reporter construct (Figure 6D) or S100a9 reporter construct (Figure 6F) together with 3xFlag-C/EBPδ vector led to enhanced GFP expression upon doxycycline treatment in comparison to co-transfection with backbone plasmid (TRE_ctrl).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Two sites within the S100a8 promoter region (site 2 and site 3) caused a reduced or absent GFP expression upon co-transfection when deleted.
source: Two sites within the S100a8 promoter region, stated as site 2 and site 3 (Figure 6E), and one within the S100a9 promoter region, stated as site 4 (Figure 6G), caused a reduced or absent GFP expression upon co-transfection when deleted.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6E.

claim: One site within the S100a9 promoter region (site 4) caused a reduced or absent GFP expression upon co-transfection when deleted.
source: Two sites within the S100a8 promoter region, stated as site 2 and site 3 (Figure 6E), and one within the S100a9 promoter region, stated as site 4 (Figure 6G), caused a reduced or absent GFP expression upon co-transfection when deleted.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6G.

claim: The functional C/EBPδ-binding sites were located within the S100a8 and S100a9 promoter regions where C/EBPδ binding was confirmed by ChIP.
source: These binding sites, in turn, were located within the S100a8 and S100a9 promoter regions where C/EBPδ binding was confirmed by ChIP (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and references Figure 6A.

claim: ATAC-seq revealed over 1000 regions with differential peaks in all comparisons between precursor and differentiated WT and C/EBPδ KO ER-Hoxb8 cells.
source: This revealed over 1000 regions with differential peaks in all comparisons (Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Among the regions with significantly higher ATAC-seq reads in differentiated samples at day 3 of WT cells were the S100a8 and S100a9 promoter and enhancer locations.
source: Among the regions with significantly higher ATAC-seq reads in differentiated samples at day 3 of WT cells were the S100a8 and S100a9 promoter and enhancer locations.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7B, C.

claim: Within S100a8 and S100a9 promoter regions, chromatin accessibility was significantly decreased in C/EBPδ KO in comparison to WT cells at day 3 of differentiation.
source: Interestingly, within these regions chromatin accessibility was significantly decreased in C/EBPδ KO in comparison to WT cells at day 3 of differentiation (Figure 7B, C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7B, C.

claim: H3K27 acetylation was increased at differentiation day 3 in monocytes over precursor cells at S100a8 loci in both WT and C/EBPδ KO cells.
source: H3K27 acetylation (H3K27ac), a marker for active transcription, was increased at differentiation day 3 in monocytes over precursor cells at S100a8 (Figure 7D) and S100a9 loci (Figure 7E) in both, WT and C/EBPδ KO cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The ER-Hoxb8 cell system reflects reliably the differentiation of myeloid progenitor cells to bone marrow-derived monocytes and macrophages.
source: The ER-Hoxb8 cell system serves as a substitute for murine primary cells of myeloid origin that can be differentiated into phagocytes, such as monocytes and neutrophils. It reflects reliably the differentiation of myeloid progenitor cells to bone marrow-derived monocytes and macrophages.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an assessment of the cell system used.

claim: Serum concentrations of alarmins correlate with disease severity and activity in several inflammatory diseases.
source: The serum concentrations of alarmins correlate with disease severity and activity and, hence, they are reliable biomarkers for monitoring several inflammatory diseases (Foell et al., 2004; Ehrchen et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Foell et al., 2004 and Ehrchen et al., 2009.

claim: S100A8/A9 expression is the first predictive marker for disease relapses in juvenile rheumatoid arthritis patients.
source: In the context of human RA, the expression and serum concentrations of S100A8/A9 correlate very well with disease activity and are the first predictive marker for disease relapses in juvenile patients, and of the responses to therapy in juvenile and adult patients (Moncrieffe et al., 2013; Choi et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Moncrieffe et al., 2013 and Choi et al., 2015.

claim: In S100A9 KO mice, neutrophil recruitment in the lung was impeded in an acute lung inflammation model.
source: In S100A9 KO mice, neutrophil recruitment in the lung was impeded when using the same mouse model (Chakraborty et al., 2017), suggesting that S100A8/A9 expression mediates effects of C/EBPδ as a key mediator of LPS-induced lung inflammation (Yan et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Chakraborty et al., 2017.

claim: C/EBPδ is a key mediator of LPS-induced lung inflammation.

evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Yan et al., 2013.

claim: C/EBPδ represents a promising target for modulation of inflammatory conditions that are characterized by S100a8 and S100a9 overexpression.
source: Therefore, C/EBPδ represents a promising target for modulation of inflammatory conditions that are characterized by S100a8 and S100a9 overexpression.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a conclusion drawn from the study findings.

claim: C/EBPδ binding to specific sites on S100a8 and S100a9 promoter regions induces changes in chromatin accessibility via JMJD3-mediated demethylation of H3K27me3 marks.
source: We found that the transcription factor C/EBPδ drives expression of the abundant alarmins S100A8 and S100A9, and demonstrated that C/EBPδ binding to specific sites on S100a8 and S100a9 promoter regions also induced changes in chromatin accessibility via JMJD3-mediated demethylation of H3K27me3 marks, which includes a so far unknown link.
evidence: This is stated in the Conclusion section and supported by data in Figures 6-8.

claim: The link between C/EBPδ and JMJD3-mediated demethylation of H3K27me3 was previously unknown.
